notes.J3.1.fair-rotation.U: Thin against backend B2.turn.rotation: the real turns worker names the longest-waiting eligible subject and the creator's screen shows that friend. Creator rotation across days is backend-only; the server clock cannot move.
notes.J3.2.offline-truth.U: A pick request failed at the gateway, with both quiet repeats, is never shown as saved; a retry saves exactly one. A reply lost after the server applied the pick is not staged.
notes.J3.3.confidence-boundaries.U: Slider ends save as 0.01 and 1; out-of-range confidence, a third option and a stake field are refused by the real handler.
notes.J3.3.concurrent-version.U: The screen converges on the pick the server accepted from another device and offers no edit; a change is refused with CONFLICT.
notes.J3.4.boundary-writes.U: A confirmation retried from the real screen after the reveal is refused and never shown as saved. The reveal is reached by moving the fixture bet's timestamps, not to the millisecond.
notes.J4.2.countdown-reactions.U: The subject's sealed card counts down to the server's reveal time and shows how many friends are in, with no question or side.
notes.J4.3.neutral-old-open.U: Thin against backend V0.quiet-veto: a vetoed bet opens as a neutral unavailable card from the open screen and from the list. Opening an old card from the transcript needs delivery and is not exercised.
notes.J5.1.resume-refresh.U: Reopening the extension after Messages was in the background reads the server again with the link intact and shows the reveal. The simulator's Messages closes the extension when it leaves the foreground, so a surviving view refreshing in place is not proven.
notes.J5.2.minority-tie-majority.U: Challenges of 1 of 3, 1 of 2 and 2 of 3 made on screen: minority and tie finalize with the answer, the majority voids, and the board shows the resulting points.
notes.J5.2.deadline-race.U: Thin against backend B4.deadline.challenge.0/.1: the open screen follows the server when the hour ends and a late challenge is refused. The millisecond boundary and a tap on a stale button are backend-only.
notes.J5.2.exactly-once-finalize.U: Thin against backend B4.finalize.exactly-once and B3.ledger.exactly-once: repeated sweeps leave one result, and the board shows the same points.
notes.J5.3.late-answer-race.U: Thin against backend B4.timeout.worker-first: the open answer screen becomes unavailable at the deadline and a late answer is refused. Only the worker-first order is shown.
notes.J5.3.single-terminal-state.U: Thin against backend B4.finalize.void-is-terminal and B4.timeout.no-answer: after the void, a late answer and more sweeps, the bet stays voided and unscored on screen and on the server.
notes.J5.5.cancel-truth.U: A prepared result card removed from the message field leaves the bet screen unchanged and nothing claims delivery. A sent card cannot be compared: the simulator sends nothing.
notes.J6.1.subject-source.U: Every idea carries the chosen subject and is labelled as template or group history; an unedited idea is stored with that source.
notes.J6.1.editable.U: A chosen idea fills the form, is edited, and is stored with the edited question and source manual.
notes.J6.1.yes-no.U: Thin against backend B1.create.format.yes_no.manual: the yes/no form asks for no line or choices and stores Yes / No.
notes.J6.1.context-private.U: Typed context is stored with the bet, absent from the Messages accessibility tree after the draft card is inserted, and absent from what other members' lists return.
notes.J6.1.tap-count.U: Group home to draft card in three taps, counted by the test. Send in Messages would be a fourth and cannot be done on a simulator.
notes.J6.2.safe-timeout-fallback.U: Thin for the provider part against backend J6.2.fallback.* and V0.suggestions.hosted-unavailable-fallback: a failed suggestion request leaves the screen usable and asking again brings safe templates. Hosted AI is off in V0, so a provider timeout cannot be driven from the screen.
notes.J6.2.no-stale-subject.U: Switching subject removes the previous subject's ideas each time.
notes.J6.3.filter-categories.U: Thin against backend J6.3.history-filter.*: settled bets in five refused categories are not offered while a safe one is.
notes.J6.3.malformed-output.U: Thin against backend J6.3.malformed-history.*: three malformed stored shapes are not offered.
notes.J6.3.nonmember.U: Thin against backend V0.suggestions.denied-role.outsider and cross-group-subject: the subject menu offers no outsider, and the real function refuses both directions.
notes.J6.3.self-subject-denied.U: Thin against backend V0.suggestions.denied-role.subject: nobody is offered themselves as subject or ideas about themselves.
notes.J6.3.group-history.U: A settled bet from another group the creator belongs to is never offered in this group.
notes.J7.1.approved-oracle.U: Thin against backend B3.oracle.*, B3.ledger.finalize and B3.ledger.streak-across-bets: three real settlements show the approved points and streaks on the home line, board and group list. Not the whole table or the x2 cap.
notes.J7.1.rounding-ties.U: 38.5 shows as 39; members level on points share a rank and are listed by name.
notes.J7.1.void-missed.U: Thin against backend B3.ledger.void.* and B3.ledger.skipped: voided and missed bets between two correct picks leave the streak alone on screen. Veto and subject-left voids are not exercised here.
notes.J7.1.exactly-once.U: Thin against backend B3.ledger.exactly-once: after retries and repeated sweeps the board and history show the result once.
notes.J7.2.group-history.U: Each group's board history shows only its own settled bets.
notes.J7.2.no-global-wallet.U: Thin against backend V0.no-foreign-board and B3.ledger.per-group: one balance per group on screen and no combined total anywhere.
notes.J7.4.group-progress.U: Thin against backend B5.progress.group-points: points earned after the goal became active move it, earlier points do not, and it reads reached past its target.
notes.J8.1.every-create-path.U: Typed text, an earlier suggestion, a refresh, the turn and the subject picker are all closed once the subject opts out. Hosted AI is cut, so there is no AI create path.
notes.J8.2.cancel-subject-bets.U: Leaving through Settings voids the open bet about the leaver and their open pick, and leaves settled and unrelated bets alone.
notes.J8.3.delete-context-proof-picks.U: Thin against backend V0.delete-cascade: deleting through Settings removes the account's bets with their context and its picks. The proof part is not proven: proof is cut from V0.
notes.J8.3.idempotent-delete.U: A delete whose reply is lost is repeated by the app and by another session and changes nothing further. Provider-cleanup reruns are backend-only (J8.3.idempotent.repeat-request).
notes.J8.4.saved-error-state.U: Settings shows a saved line or an error, never both, across a failed save, a success, a refusal and a report.
notes.J9.1.one-use-expiring-invite.U: An invitation that expires on screen is refused; one accepted admits once; reuse is refused. Expiry is reached by moving the invitation's timestamps; the boundary instant is backend V0.invite-expiry.
notes.J9.2.no-old-history.U: After rejoining the screen shows 0 points and none of the earlier bets. Replaying old card links needs delivery; that part is thin against backend V0.history-rejoin.
notes.J9.2.no-old-token-settlement.U: Thin against backend J9.2.no-settlement-after-leave.challenge and CONFIRM.rejoin-old-interval-denied: the open bet closes on the leaver's screen and a challenge from before the leave is refused, also after rejoining.
notes.J9.2.cascade.U: Leaving closes the membership, expires the turn, revokes the sent invitation and removes the link; rejoining opens a new membership at 0.
notes.SEC1.public-export-policy.U: Thin against backend V0.policy-inventory and SEC1.policy-source: the gateway forwards only inventoried public functions and refused none of the app's calls on the screens visited. The inventory itself is a source contract with no screen.
notes.SEC1.read-matrix.U: Signed-out and outsider views show nothing of the group. Thin for the rest of the matrix against backend SEC1.matrix-inventory and V0.scope.*; foreign-id probes cannot be entered through the UI.
notes.SEC1.eligible-members.U: Thin against backend V0.eligible.friend: a friend sees the question and options and none of the other picks, context or controls. The creator's view is backend-only.
notes.SEC1.subject-lock.U: Thin against backend V0.subject.*: the subject's list, board and bet screen show only the sealed card until the server reveals.
notes.SEC1.revocation.U: Thin against backend SEC2.session-revoked and revoke-all-devices: a sign-in revoked elsewhere clears the open bet to sign-in in the extension, and the host app, coming back to the foreground, shows the phone sign-in by itself.
notes.SEC1.membership-interval.U: Thin against backend V0.current-member-boundary: leaving removes the open question and rejoining brings back no earlier bet or points.
notes.SEC2.wrong-expired-replay.U: Wrong and expired codes are refused on screen with no session. Replay is not proven natively: the app discards the challenge on success, so the screen cannot resubmit it; backend SEC2.otp-replay is the only evidence for that part.
notes.SEC2.bounded-attempts.U: After five wrong codes the right one is refused and never reaches the provider. Hourly and global quotas are backend-only.
notes.SEC2.stable-account.U: Signing in again with the same phone lands on the same account, groups and points. A second device is not possible on one simulator.
notes.SEC2.session-revocation.U: Thin against backend SEC2.revoke-one-device and revoke-all-devices: a revoked sign-in and an ordinary sign-out both end the session and its conversation link, extension first and host first (at a return to the foreground and at a cold launch).
notes.SEC2.no-username-admission.U: Taking a member's display name admits nobody: the group is still not offered and the board does not merge the accounts.
notes.SEC3.locked-fields.U: Thin against backend V0.subject.*: nothing but locked metadata on screen or in the accessibility tree before the reveal. The MSMessage payload is SEC3.shared-payload-scan, which stays blocked.
notes.SEC3.stale-cache-clear.U: A question already on screen is removed when the sign-in is revoked or the membership ends, and after the host alone met the refusal the reopened extension shows nothing and calls nothing. Messages is relaunched to reopen it; the app-switcher snapshot cannot be inspected from a UI test.
notes.J1.1.consenting-subject.U: Thin against backend B1.create.subject-withdrawn.no-bets and B1.create.app-named-subject: a friend who opts out while the form is open cannot be made the subject and is no longer offered; choosing another subject than the app named is refused.
notes.J1.3.idempotent-create.U: A create applied three times with its reply lost, then retried by hand, makes one bet under one request id; a double tap sends one request. Backend side is B1.create.idempotent.
notes.J1.3.cancel-resume.U: A staged card removed with Messages' own control leaves one open bet, and the card can be prepared again from it with no second create. No backend test is bound to this line.
notes.J2.2.logout-expiry.U: Signing out in either app signs the other out, and a sign-in expired on the server ends the session in both. Backend side is SEC2.revoke-one-device and SEC2.session-expired. Expiry by the device clock is not exercised.
notes.J3.1.noon-pass.U: The product turns job passes an unused turn once after noon group time, the first creator is no longer offered it, and the member it passed to makes the one bet of the day. Noon is reached by moving the fixture group zone and the turn timestamps, not the clock, so the exact 12:00 boundary stays with backend B2.turn.noon-pass.
